2026-WAOWF-260406.t: 40 homes and structures destroyed, per the Washington emergency operations report of September 24. An earlier county survey of the upper Entiat Valley counted at least 35, including 2 primary homes and 13 cabins.

2026-CALPF-002271.t: One minor structure destroyed as of August 27, with assessment still under way, per the incident management team.

2026-WANES-001791.t: 31 homes and structures destroyed, per the Washington emergency operations report of September 24.

2026-ORMHF-000688.t: At least 6 homes and about 15 outbuildings destroyed.

2026-COCUX-001160.t: 319 homes destroyed (241 in Pueblo County, 78 in Custer County), per the county sheriffs' assessments as of July 17. One estimate put all structures lost at 780 to 851.

2026-ORMHF-000863.t: A worker removing hazard trees was injured on the fire and later died.

2026-ORVAD-260201.t: An estimated 13 to 15 structures lost on the Idaho side, along with significant livestock losses, as of July 29.
s: Idaho Statesman via East Idaho News

2026-CALPF-002475.t: No structures reported destroyed as of August 27.

2026-WAOWF-260420.t: No homes or structures destroyed, per the Washington emergency operations report of September 24.

2026-UTMLF-005112.t: Five structures destroyed as of July 17.

2026-UTFIF-260198.t: Almost 150 homes destroyed, plus lodges and ski lifts at Eagle Point Resort, as reported July 9. The report does not name the source of the count.

2026-WACOA-260140.t: At least 20 structures destroyed and one firefighter injured, as of August 17.

2026-CAYNP-000100.t: Two pilots died when a firefighting helicopter crashed.

2026-NMSNF-000444.t: A fire crew member died while assigned to the fire.

2026-ORFWF-260286.t: A dozer operator died while working the fire.
